title: Network Monitoring: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A building manager watches every room from one screen. They get readings, and alarms when something breaks. S N M P does that for networks.

scenes.heading: The control room
scenes.narration: S N M P has two ways to hear from a device. Polling means the manager asks for a reading. A trap is the device shouting that something happened. Only version three has real security. Old community strings are public for read and private for write.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Quick facts. Traps use one sixty two. Community strings are plaintext. Only version three is secure.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Polls are on one sixty one, and traps are on one sixty two. A trap is an alert from the device. Use version three for security. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva monitoring lab.
